Title: Futures Decrease Tuesday

Summary: 
Canada's main stock index futures declined on Tuesday as commodity prices dropped sharply, with investors awaiting central bank rate decisions and a wave of corporate earnings. Market sentiment improved on Monday amid cooling U.S.-China tensions ahead of a high-profile meeting between President Donald Trump and President Xi Jinping, with both nations agreeing on a framework for a potential trade deal covering rare earth minerals, soybean purchases, and TikTok. The U.S. government shutdown has created an economic data blackout. Investors are also focused on upcoming earnings from 'Magnificent Seven' stocks—Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta Platforms, and Microsoft—accounting for roughly a quarter of the S&P 500’s value. So far, Q3 earnings have started strongly. Amazon announced it would begin the largest workforce layoffs in its history on Tuesday, adding to recent tech industry job cuts.

Title: STACY BUSH: Why this September could defy a tough trend - Valdosta Daily Times

Summary: 
The article, written by Stacy Bush for the Valdosta Daily Times, analyzes why September 2025 could break its historically negative pattern. When the S&P 500 is above this threshold in September, the average return jumps to +1.3 % with 60 % positive outcomes; below it, the average decline is 4.2 %.  The article also points out that a green August typically leads to a 3.2 % September gain, whereas a red August predicts a 3.8 % loss.  Despite the strong August, the author cautions that implied volatility (VIX) is at year‑to‑date lows, and political and macroeconomic uncertainties could increase turbulence.  The recommendation for long‑term investors is to stay diversified and maintain a long‑term horizon, while short‑term traders should be aware of the historical weakness but also the higher odds of gains when momentum is positive. Title: Wall Street set to decline following last week's records, fueled by the Fed's first rate cut of 2025

Summary: 
Wall Street opened lower on Monday after a record‑setting week that included the Federal Reserve’s first interest‑rate cut of 2025. Market participants are focusing on forthcoming Fed speeches rather than the latest inflation data. New Trump‑appointed Fed official Stephen Miran will present his views at the Economic Club of New York on Monday, while Powell is scheduled to speak in Providence, Rhode Island on Tuesday. In equities, T‑Mobile shares fell 1.2% after announcing that COO Srini Gopalan would replace Mike Sievert as CEO; Sievert was moved to a newly created management role. Pfizer shares dropped 1.6% after announcing a $4.9 billion purchase of development‑stage obesity drugmaker Metsera, which has no market products but has four clinical programs and one mid‑stage test. Internationally, France’s CAC 40 slipped 0.1%, Germany’s DAX fell 0.6%, and Britain’s FTSE 100 edged up less than 0.1%. In Asia, Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 1.0% to 45,493.66, rebounding from a late‑week decline over concerns about the Bank of Japan’s asset sales. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 gained 0.4% to 8,810.90, South Korea’s Kospi rose 0.7% to 3,468.65, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng fell 0.8% to 26,344.14, and Shanghai Composite rose 0.2% to 3,828.58.
